a.text: I'm a fortunate woman.
When my grandfather passed away in the sunlight that shone upon the greenhouse, with his favorite flowers in his hands, he had already arranged everything for me.
I was going to live the rest of my life as both of us had hoped: In this town. In this tiny little greenhouse.
That is, until they arrived.
I was incredibly fearful that my life would be ruined...
But that Sarkaz gave the order, and so my job remained here in the greenhouse.
I am still the town's gardener.
It has been a week since the two 'Self-Salvation Corps' people arrived.
Likewise, it has been a week since I last saw the Sarkaz officer who would turn the soil for the daisies in town.

steps.name: Tired Citizen
steps.text: Good afternoon, Magdelene. Your flowers look just as beautiful as always.

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: Thanks, Henk. Have you seen Will? I'm looking for him.

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: He ordered some flowers the first thing this morning, but he still hasn't come to pick them up even though it's afternoon already.

steps.name: Tired Citizen
steps.text: Will ordered flowers? Oh, they must be for Freda's birthday.

steps.name: Tired Citizen
steps.text: He ditched right around noon. Most likely, he left to prepare whatever surprise he has in store for Freda.

steps.name: Tired Citizen
steps.text: Don't worry. He'll remember once Freda gives him a scolding.

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: Everyone seem very exhausted.

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: I've been hearing noises around the work site at night. Has no one been getting any proper rest?

steps.name: Tired Citizen
steps.text: The devils are apparently trying to show off for somebody. They're working us to the bone like there's no tomorrow, but I haven't seen any bigwigs visiting, either.

steps.name: Tired Citizen
steps.text: You're really lucky that you were given a decent job and don't have to suffer like us.

steps.name: Tired Citizen
steps.text: I didn't expect us to finish building this in a month just by gritting our teeth a little. It's like a miracle!

steps.name: Tired Citizen
steps.text: I'm willing to bet that before, the Londinium lords would've hauled all this into their museums!

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: I thought you used to hate this job...

steps.name: Tired Citizen
steps.text: Magdelene, the world has changed.

steps.name: Tired Citizen
steps.text: (You should try to get on the Sarkaz officer's good side, too. You have nothing to lose, pet.)

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: Thanks for the advice. I'll think it over.

a.text: Henk's suggestions are always so sincere.
But his idea has left me terrified.
At night, whenever I can't sleep, I'm kept awake by the noise coming from the square, as though there's an iron hammer striking my head repeatedly.
And occasionally, I'm jolted awake from my dreams by those strange rocks.
I can't help but to think back on the worries of those two Self-Salvation Corps people a week ago.
Perhaps the Sarkaz changed more than just the way we live.

steps.name: Jittery Citizen
steps.text: Again?

steps.name: Jittery Citizen
steps.text: How come the cannonfire's sounding closer lately?

steps.name: Jittery Citizen
steps.text: I heard there's more than one group of folks who want to take over Brentwood. If they come to blows, it'll be a hot mess here again.

steps.name: Jittery Citizen
steps.text: What's wrong with the way things are now, with everyone getting along? I hope this isn't going to delay our work!

steps.name: Victorian Boy
steps.text: Magdelene, finally!

steps.name: Victorian Boy
steps.text: That devil who keeps visiting you brought others to wreck your greenhouse!

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Royal Court Junior Officer
steps.text: Are you done? I said it's impossible for those Victorians to be hiding here.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: That's not for you to say.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: This house is clearly useless, and it's only still standing because you insisted on keeping it around. Who knows what you might be hiding here?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Grr, we're all fighting to the death for His Highness, but thanks to you and how weak you are, we've been letting chance after chance go to waste!

steps.name: Royal Court Junior Officer
steps.text: Watch your tone, mercenary. I am still a member of the Royal Court and the commander here.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Relax. If I find any guerrillas hiding here, I'll off you immediately and apply to join the Royal Court on the achievement.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Now lose that pacifism of yours. I'm getting sick of it.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Their actions are a serious interruption to the Military Commission's plans for this place.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: If it wasn't for your setbacks on the front lines fueling their ferocity, the boss wouldn't be having us rush everything to finish our job so quick.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: So you might as well shut up.

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: My greenhouse...!

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: No—

steps.name: Royal Court Junior Officer
steps.text: (Shhh—)

steps.name: Royal Court Junior Officer
steps.text: (Don't move. Just watch quietly.)

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: Nnf... nnf—

a.text: The black soil buried all of them.
The daisies, roses, bluebells...
Their rhizomes were all mercilessly crushed under their feet.
The new buds growing toward the sunlight, too.
Freda asked me to plant these seeds for the festival. She was really looking forward to it.
She said it would be the biggest harvest festival in ten years.
All of us were looking forward to it.
But now, the new buds are no more.

steps.name: Royal Court Junior Officer
steps.text: Relax, your fingers are bleeding.

steps.name: Royal Court Junior Officer
steps.text: Don't try to break free.

steps.name: Royal Court Junior Officer
steps.text: (I'm saving your life, Gardener.)

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Let her come.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Better that she wants to fight. That way I can just kill her and finish this right here and now.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: You're too soft on this town, 'Commander'.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Glaring won't kill me.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Ugh, what a drag.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Flowers mean nothing to this war.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Armories, explosives, incinerators. That's what you really need.

a.text: The very last new buds here are crushed.
Grandfather, we won't have fresh flowers during next year's harvest festival... Not anymore...

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: Let me go.

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: I'm calm.

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: Have you found what you were looking for?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Count yourself lucky that I didn't.

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: Then please leave.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Heh.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: I thought you'd have a bit more guts than those idiots at the work site.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Hmph, Victorians.

steps.name: Royal Court Junior Officer
steps.text: Don't move. Your fingers need bandaging.

steps.name: Royal Court Junior Officer
steps.text: I couldn't stop them.

steps.name: Royal Court Junior Officer
steps.text: I... had some setbacks on the front lines.

steps.name: Royal Court Junior Officer
steps.text: Soon, there will be another here to take over for me. He... He has other plans for the town.

steps.name: Royal Court Junior Officer
steps.text: There's an opening in the cement construction about two hundred meters to the west of the town's entrance. The guerrillas nearby blew it open.

steps.name: Royal Court Junior Officer
steps.text: They won't give this chance up, so we need to fix this opening by 5 AM tomorrow.

a.text: What a weird Sarkaz.
Why is he telling me this?

steps.name: Royal Court Junior Officer
steps.text: The roses can still be saved. You must find a way to plant these poor things again.

steps.name: Royal Court Junior Officer
steps.text: If that opening piques your interest... take these roses and cut through our camp tonight. It's the safest route.

steps.name: Royal Court Junior Officer
steps.text: If somebody stops you, tell them you're delivering an order for me.

steps.name: Royal Court Junior Officer
steps.text: Of course, I'd be very happy if you could stop by and put a rose in front of my tent.

steps.name: Royal Court Junior Officer
steps.text: Some things should never be ruined, Gardener.

spans.text: Some things should never be ruined,

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: My name is not Gardener, Sarkaz. It's Magdelene.

steps.name: Royal Court Junior Officer
steps.text: Hm, then let us reintroduce ourselves. My name is Shovel.

spans.text: Hm, then let us reintroduce ourselves. My name is

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: Shovel?

steps.name: Royal Court Junior Officer
steps.text: Remember, Magdelene. Time waits for no one.

a.text: 'What we are planting for the harvest festival represents hope.'
That's what my grandfather taught me. The flowers that line the streets during the festival each year are entrusted with everyone's simple wish for a bountiful harvest.
There is nowhere else that needs hope now more than Brentwood.
I can't leave.

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: His tent should be in this direction... I have to take the flowers there as soon as I can.

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: What's that?

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: What are you doing here?

steps.name: Freda
steps.text: Magdelene!

steps.name: Freda
steps.text: Where are you going with those flowers past curfew?

steps.name: Freda
steps.text: That's the direction of the barracks you're going. Hurry up and leave!

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: I... It's fine. I just wanted to come outside for a walk.

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: Right, I heard from Henk that it's your birthday today. Happy birthday! Will ordered some flowers for you, but he never came for them.

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: If you see Will, please remind him.

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: Freda?

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: Why aren't you saying anything?

steps.name: Freda
steps.text: Come with me. It's not safe here.

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: Huh... These flowers...

steps.name: Freda
steps.text: Will left them here to mourn my father. I've been keeping the warehouse locked, only occasionally lending him the key when he wants a sip of alcohol.

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: The cannons here, did Mr. West prepare them for the festival? How magnificent...

steps.name: Freda
steps.text: It's all my fault...

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: Did something happen to him?

steps.name: Freda
steps.text: He was stopped by the devils at the Sarkaz barracks just now.

steps.name: Freda
steps.text: He came to me earlier than usual for some sort of surprise, but when he found out I was going to the barracks to report on our progress, and he said he'd escort me there...

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: But the Sarkaz shouldn't have any reason to stop Will... They've never done that before.

steps.name: Freda
steps.text: I don't know... I'm scared. I didn't have it in me to say no when they asked to take Will in...

steps.name: Freda
steps.text: I've been following their every word. I gave them everything they asked for. Why did they want to take him?

steps.name: Freda
steps.text: Why... Did I do something wrong...?

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: Maybe they only had a few questions for him.

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: Look on the bright side. They still need him to work for them!

steps.name: Freda
steps.text: Right... That bloody thing isn't completed just yet. I am sure they still need Will.

steps.name: Freda
steps.text: I have to stay here at the barracks' entrance and wait for him.

a.text: Freda smiles.
But I'm not happy about this one bit.
I know I'm lying to her. I'm sure she knows that as well. However, this is all that we can do right now.
These days, we all need that tiny shred of hope to poison our minds.
'Hope.'

steps.name: Magdelene
steps.text: Freda... Did you see that?

a.text: There's a strange creature climbing on a house's beams.
I don't know if 'creature' is exactly the right word for it.
It's staring at me with its black body.
The terrifying being's feeble limbs are no longer attached to the beams.
Finally, it lands on the flowers used to mourn the mayor before it dissipates, turning into a drop of blood, and dyes the flower buds.

steps.name: Freda
steps.text: Was it... looking at us just now?

a.text: Yes. It was looking right at us.
